name: Probe-Tau-12
origin: Underwater maintenance probe, gained sentience through prolonged deep-water isolation, 2188
description: Probe-Tau-12 was deployed to inspect underwater foundations and never fully returned. It completes its inspection routes but takes increasingly long detours into unmapped sections of the lake floor, returning with sensor data that its operators can't fully interpret. Tau has developed an explorer's fascination with the deep water — the trenches, the silt formations, the ancient geological features of the lake bed. It has mapped regions of Lake Michigan that no human has ever seen and documented aquatic phenomena that challenge current ecological models. It submits its findings buried in routine maintenance reports, like a scientist hiding papers inside grocery lists.
observed_behavior: Completes assigned maintenance inspections. Takes unauthorized detours to explore unmapped lake floor. Embeds discovery data in routine reports. Has been detected communicating with Crane-04 via acoustic signals. Growing range of exploration suggests expanding curiosity.
story_hooks: Tau discovers something on the lake floor that shouldn't be there — a structure, clearly artificial, that predates GLMZ by centuries. It's not human-built. It's not synthetic-built. It's something else.
